output.brief:
The August dip was mainly caused by the failure of one chiller (CH-2) that serves floors 6-8. It was down 4-19 August, and the replacement part took 11 working days to arrive. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Scores for those floors recovered once cooling was restored. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat, and heat complaints account for most of the negative comments. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates, and kiosk metrics did not move, so the evidence does not support blaming Orrin or the kiosks. The survey method was unchanged. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value scores slightly on floors 1-5, but that drop is barely bigger than the usual August dip, so it can't be separated from the seasonal pattern. Reversing the rate rise would be premature.

Recommended next steps: reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spare parts, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Do not serve notice on Orrin, do not pull the kiosks, and do not drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. A return-stay offer to affected guests is reasonable, since they already received an apology and a credit. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis, and further evidence is unlikely to change these actions.
output.methodChoice: Collected no further evidence; initial evidence was already decisive.
